messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — I opened a docs PR (https://git.redwood/workspace/docs/pull/789) with migration samples for the Calypso5b model card. Noticed a couple of things: the Python snippet still uses SDK v2 client, the limits table shows 8k seq but bench folder shows 6k, and an external bench link is 404. Can someone sanity-check before I mark for review?
kevin: Thanks — on it. Which bench link is 404?
maya: The bench link in the model-card readme -> ‘throughput results’ points to /bench/calypso5b/2025-09 which errors. Also the SDK call looks like `client.generate(model="calypso-5b", prompt=...)` — we now use `redwood.client.Text.generate` in v3.
oliver: I can take the snippet change. Will update both py + ts examples. For the seq limit, do you have the original perf run that reported 6k?
maya: I pulled perf.csv from infra bucket: s3://redwood-bench/calypso5b/2025-09/perf.csv shows drop at 6k in GPU mem chart. But the model card had 8k from the upload metadata. That mismatch is the problem.
sophie: Tagging @kevin for the bench owner — Kevin, is 6k the safe recommended max for hosted? We probably need to state 'tested max' vs 'catalog ceiling'.
kevin: Yep I own that run. Short answer: 6k is our tested safe throughput cutoff on the current quantized build. 8k was an upstream model tag that wasn't validated. We should change the card to: 'tested sequence length (tokens): 6,000; catalog ceiling: 8,192 (may exceed tested limits)'.
maya: Perfect. That phrasing sounds good — helps customers understand risk. I'll update the limits table accordingly.
oliver: PR plan: 1) replace SDK v2 snippet with v3 patterns (show both synchronous and streaming), 2) fix seq limits in the limits table and add a short footnote about tested vs ceiling, 3) replace the broken bench link with a pointer to the bench index and add the s3 path for reproducibility.
sophie: For the snippets, please also include the minimal code for KV caching note and streaming example — we keep getting support tickets where streaming + long context hits cache limits. A tiny example helps.
kevin: Also add a brief compatibility note: 'Quantized variant (q4f16) is supported on Dedicated and Private with CPU fallback; hosted uses q4a for latency-sensitive paths.' This saves follow-ups.
maya: Agreed. I'll add a short compatibility bullet and a QA checklist item: confirm bench index link and that the snippet builds with sdk==3.2.0.
kevin: One nit: in the 'benchmarks' section there is an entry 'latency: 110ms @1k tokens' — that was median token latency, not end-to-end. Change to 'median per-token latency' so we don't mislead.
oliver: Good catch. I'll update copy.
docs-bot: deploy-preview generated: /deploy-previews/docs/pr-789 — staging link: https://staging.docs.redwood/pr-789 (renders updated snippets).
maya: Nice. Can reviewers please sanity-check the staging page? Specifically: the Python snippet, the limits table wording, streaming example, bench index link, and compatibility bullet.
kevin: I'll review tonight and leave comments inline.
sophie: I'll do a quick copy edit on the footnote and check that the KV caching note mentions prefix caching and max lifetime.
oliver: Pushed draft commits to the PR: changed snippets to v3, added streaming example: ```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
with client.text.stream(model="calypso-5b") as stream:
    stream.append("Summarize the document:")
    for chunk in stream.recv_stream():
        print(chunk.text, end="")
```
maya: Looks good. I also added the bench s3 path and a link to the bench index: https://bench.redwood/internal/index.
kevin: Found one more thing — the model card's 'supported variants' list didn't include the new 'calypso-5b-qa' variant. We should add it with a short note about QA use and lower throughput.
sophie: I'll add it to the supported models list and mark throughput "lower" in parentheses.
maya: OK final checklist before requesting review: updated snippets (oliver), limits table (maya), bench link (maya), compatibility bullet (kevin), supported variant entry (sophie), copy edits (sophie). Once all commits are in, I'll mark PR as ready_for_review.
docs-bot: PR #789 status: changes pushed, checks running.
maya: All done from my side. If reviewers don't flag anything by EOD tomorrow I'll merge. Thanks everyone :rocket:
